bullets.title: AI/Tech selloff deepens: October recap shows NDX -6.7%, neoclouds -35%, semis -18%
bullets.body: JPM's October market intelligence recap shows MSCI ACWI -1.7%, NDX -6.7%, SPX -0.9%, with global hedge funds down ~4% across all regions. The AI/tech unwind drove a sharp momentum reversal—defensives outperformed cyclicals by 23pp (defensives +9.6%, cyclicals -13.4%)—while North Asia saw massive foreign selling ($15B Korea, $32B Taiwan). Neoclouds led declines at -35.3% after a CoreWeave CDS spike, semis -18%, memory -26%.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: Market correction in 'final inning'; Hedgeye calls for Nasdaq >20% drawdown by Q2 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Michael Wilson podcast characterizes the equity correction as entering its final phase ahead of midterms. Hedgeye's McCullough is more bearish, forecasting a Nasdaq decline exceeding 20% by Q2 2027 in a 'Quad 4' downturn, with Nasdaq volatility in the 'F-Bucket' and short-dated vol in the 20s potentially reaching 30s. McCullough is long bonds, long RSP (equal-weight S&P), and short concentrated tech/AI names including NBIS, CRWV, and IREN.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: options price ~90bp SPX move; historical pattern is +14-15% S&P over next 6 months
bullets.body: JPM's midterm toolkit puts options-implied SPX move at ~90bps (similar to an average NFP print). Historically, the S&P has risen an average 14.5-16.4% from end-August to end-March in midterm election years with a 100% six- to twelve-month hit rate since 1990. Blue Wave (66% prob) presents AI regulation risk but limited SPX impact; Red Wave (7% prob) could push long-end yields higher while SPX gains 1-1.25%.

bullets.title: September JOLTS beats across the board; vacancy/unemployed ratio no longer signals upside unemployment risk
bullets.body: September JOLTS was the strongest report of the year: job openings jumped to 7.523M vs. 7.11M estimate (+333k m/m), August revised up 111k, quits rate rose to 2.1% (highest since June 2025), and the vacancy rate climbed to 1.06 from 1.01. Morgan Stanley notes the vacancy/unemployment ratio no longer implies upside risk to unemployment, though the white-collar market remains sluggish. MS models 60k October payrolls.

bullets.title: AI capex sustainability debate intensifying: Anthropic 2027 compute costs could reach ~$117B (~90% of revenue)
bullets.body: 22V Research flags Anthropic's Q3 compute costs hit $9.9B (+77% QoQ), representing 58% of revenue; extrapolating growth implies ~$117B in 2027 theoretical compute or ~90% of estimated revenue. AI usage was lower QoQ with no cross-sector broadening, and AI Quantifiers guided to only 60bps margin improvement vs. 130bps last quarter. Broad AI baskets are expected to remain range-bound into next year given uncertain returns and high capex commitments.

bullets.title: Semi supply remains structurally tight; real prices 'skyrocketing' unlike prior cycles
bullets.body: PSC Macro notes U.S. real semi manufacturing shipments are down $6B (-23%) from 2025 peaks with inventories down $13B (-22%), driving the inventory/sales ratio down 5% from highs and putting upward pressure on prices unlike prior cycles. Imported tech product sales rose $40B while inventories rose only $15B, further compressing the I/S ratio. Separately, planned-but-not-started data center construction is showing rolloff, flagged as a potential sign of tech boom deceleration.

bullets.title: Memory undersupply persists into 2027: DRAM S/D ratio -3.8%, NAND -3.3%; server DRAM demand +53% YoY
bullets.body: Citi projects 2027E DRAM supply/demand ratio at -3.8% (easing from -8.7%) and NAND at -3.3% (from -6.1%), with memory supply/demand fulfillment currently ~70%. Server DRAM demand is projected +53% YoY and eSSD +52% YoY in 2027E, while handset DRAM is expected to decline 11% YoY. DRAM capex is being revised up +55% YoY as suppliers pursue long-term agreements rather than excessive spot pricing.

bullets.title: AAPL -4% premarket: gross margin guide 45-46% misses, Services decelerating to 8-9% in Dec quarter
bullets.body: Apple's Q4 beat on revenue ($114.48B, +~1% vs. FactSet) and EPS ($2.10 including $0.05 tariff benefit), but the Dec quarter guide is creating pressure: revenue guided +7-10% y/y (above FactSet +5.8%) while Services guided only +8-9% vs. FactSet +10%, gross margin guided 45-46% vs. consensus 46.5%, and memory costs are cited as a structural headwind worsening through FY27. At ~35-36x NTM earnings vs. a 5-year avg of 28x, GS and UBS debate whether the dip gets defended given mutual fund underweights.

bullets.title: MRVL acquires LITE in $80B all-stock deal targeting AI optical connectivity; investors skeptical, stock -13%
bullets.body: Marvell is acquiring Lumentum in an all-stock deal valuing LITE at $80B ($684/share at 4.5x MRVL shares), expected to close 1H28. Oppenheimer frames it as a vertically integrated AI connectivity platform with combined 2030 TAM expanding by $60B to $550B; LITE's InP lasers are supply-constrained into at least 2028. However, Wolfe Research notes no investors encountered favor the deal, citing cyclical optical risk and fixed-cost fab exposure added to MRVL, and questions whether LITE CEO's financial incentive signals a market top for optical.

bullets.title: Internet sector 8% lower on AI monetization concerns; GOOGL/META/AMZN now at 14-21x 2026 EPS
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley rates North America Internet Attractive after the sector fell ~8%, led by GOOGL -13%, RDDT -36%, SNAP -16%, RBLX -19%, META -4%, AMZN -3%. AMZN/GOOGL/META now trade at 18x/14x/21x 2026 EPS, down 33%/42%/3% vs. TTM averages. The sell-off reflects AI monetization skepticism and concerns about hyperscaler FCF sustainability, not earnings deterioration per 22V's regime model.

bullets.title: PLTR +96% revenue growth with 165% NRR, but flat sequential backlog raises peak-growth concern
bullets.body: Palantir delivered Q3 revenue growth of 96% YoY, US Commercial +148%, US Government +96%, with commercial surpassing government revenue for the first time. NRR improved to 165% from 157% and adj. operating margin guidance was raised to 61.5%. However, UBS flags sequential backlog was flat for the first time in 3.5 years and new logo adds decelerated from 40-45 to 33/quarter, raising questions about whether acceleration pace is peaking even as absolute growth remains strong.

bullets.title: SHOP -16% on earnings: 30% FXN GMV growth misses low-30s guidance; Q4 guided low-30s% with margin headwinds
bullets.body: Shopify's Q3 revenue was $3.74B (in line) with operating income +66% YoY to $568M and FCF of $816M, but GMV of $119.1B missed the $120B consensus and management's 'low-30s%' FXN GMV guidance came in at 30%, disappointing a long-positioned market. Q4 is guided for revenue growth in the low-30s% with FCF margin in-line with Q4 2025, but OpEx guided at 29-30% of revenue. JPM characterizes the -15% reaction as an expectations reset rather than a thesis break.

bullets.title: China A-shares: CSI-300 at 11.5x P/E after -22% drawdown; JPM recommends AI infrastructure and healthcare barbell
bullets.body: JPMorgan recommends a barbell strategy on China A-shares after CSI-300 fell 22% from June peaks to 11.5x FTM P/E (0.5 standard deviations below long-run median). Chinese authorities set a policy floor on Nov 2 via coordinated PBOC/CSRC meetings. Q3 CSI-300 earnings showed +5% SPS but -4% EPS YoY with a 60% miss ratio; 4Q26 would need 101% EPS growth to hit full-year consensus. JPM's growth picks include Huaqin, AMEC, and NAURA.

bullets.title: Anthropic's Claude targeting chip design; CDNS and SNPS trade lower on competitive threat
bullets.body: The Information reports Anthropic is emphasizing Claude's chip design capabilities to prospective IPO investors, driving CDNS and SNPS lower on concerns about potential displacement in EDA workflows. No financial specifics were provided, but the signal adds to broader AI-disruption pressure on software and tools incumbents.

bullets.title: Midterm data center policy: TX, GA, OH utility commission races could determine long-term DC buildout pace
bullets.body: Texas has a 474 GW interconnection queue (~90% data center demand) with a Dec 10 ERCOT audit as a near-term catalyst. Georgia's Democratic candidate has called for a statewide data center pause, and two of five utility commission seats are up. Ohio has 21 of 35 national data center ballot measures with utility regulator races already priced as favorites. The note argues regulatory process—not gubernatorial outcomes—will drive long-term data center policy.

bullets.title: NVDA: FT reports instruction to data center clients to make majority of clients non-Chinese
bullets.body: Pre-market reports via StreetAccount indicate NVIDIA has instructed data center clients to ensure the majority of their clients are non-Chinese, likely reflecting export control compliance pressure. NVDA was +2.3% in pre-market alongside broader semi sector strength (+3.36% for SOXX) driven by earnings results from AEHR, LSCC, and AEIS.

bullets.title: EM suffered worst October since 2018: MSCI EM -8.1%, KOSPI -16.2%, Brazil -12.1%
bullets.body: October was the worst month for EM since March 2026 and worst October since 2018: MSCI EM fell 8.1% vs. SPX -0.9%, driven by AI monetization fears hitting EM IT (-12%) and Industrials (-12%). The Philly SOX dropped 15.4% and KOSPI slumped 16.2% (now -36% from June highs). Brazil fell 12.1% on Lula's election victory; India was a notable outperformer at +1.2% on resilient earnings and relative defensiveness.

bullets.title: BofA: CTA sell trigger near Friday close; systematic positioning fell to $290B from $370B
bullets.body: BofA's morning note flagged that a CTA sell trigger activates near Friday's closing level, with a ~2% additional decline unwinding remaining longs. Systematic positioning has already fallen to $290B from a peak of $370B, indicating significant de-grossing has occurred but potential for further mechanical selling remains.

bullets.title: Oracle 86.2M share secondary priced at $116; ORCL stock was -9% cited on show date
bullets.body: Oracle priced an 86.2M share secondary offering at $116.00 per share in the Nov 3 US syndicate recap. Separately, Hedgeye noted Oracle down ~9% on the show date, consistent with broader AI infrastructure de-rating. The secondary adds supply pressure at a time when the stock faces multiple compression alongside the broader AI theme.

bullets.title: UBS post-midterm macro: SPX historically +14.5% in 6 months post-midterms; long 10s30s steepeners favored
bullets.body: UBS notes global equities are up 9% YTD 2026 despite a 10% Nasdaq decline, and the S&P has risen an average 14.5% (median 16.4%) from end-August to end-March in midterm years. Markets are increasingly pricing a Democratic sweep, limiting long-end rally scope; a Republican sweep is a tail risk for yields. UBS favors long 1y-forward 10s30s steepeners as a bullish duration trade and sees French 10y spreads reaching 150bps by end-2026.
